title: JinkoSolar claims 35.24% efficiency for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell
summary: The result was confirmed by the Shanghai Institute of Microsystem and Information Technology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The post JinkoSolar claims 35.24% efficiency for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell appeared first on pv magazine Global .

score_reasons: +3 Close, specific exposure to this company
direction_reasons: TECHNOLOGY cuts both ways — growth against capital, cost or execution risk
WAAREEENER.why_it_matters: This reaches the company through a close, specific exposure via its competitor, product exposure to JinkoSolar, and solar cells. The parts of the business most likely touched are product, competition. Classified as technology.

ai_analysis.revenue_effect: Unclear in the short term as perovskite-silicon tandem cells remain in lab/development stages; long-term revenue could face pressure in export markets if global competitors offer commercial tandem modules with significantly higher conversion efficiencies.
ai_analysis.margin_effect: Unclear in the short term; over the medium-to-long term, gross margins could compress if conventional TOPCon and PERC modules face faster price degradation due to next-generation tech commercialization.
ai_analysis.cost_effect: Input and operating costs remain unaffected in the near term, but Waaree may face higher capital expenditure and R&D expenses in the medium-to-long term to re-tool lines or adopt tandem manufacturing technology.
ai_analysis.competitive_effect: Strengthens the technology leadership position of global competitor JinkoSolar, widening the technological R&D gap for Indian manufacturers in high-efficiency export markets.
ai_analysis.regulatory_effect: No immediate regulatory effect, though it could prompt Indian policymakers to push for higher efficiency standards or offer R&D incentives under domestic manufacturing schemes.
ai_analysis.short_term: Negligible operational or financial impact over the next 0-3 months, as the efficiency claim represents a laboratory-level milestone rather than an immediate commercial product launch.
ai_analysis.medium_long_term: Increases technology obsolescence risk for current TOPCon and Mono PERC manufacturing assets over a 3 to 7 year horizon if perovskite tandem cells achieve commercial durability and scale.
ai_analysis.second_order_effects: Could accelerate strategic partnerships or licensing deals between Indian module makers and global equipment suppliers, while shifting global buyer expectations toward higher efficiency standards.
ai_analysis.key_uncertainty: The timeline and manufacturing cost required to translate JinkoSolar's lab-scale efficiency into mass-produced, commercially durable tandem modules.
